allocator_runtime_state.rationale: Allocated bytes are nearly invariant; reserved/peak correlations with latency are weak (~0.22–0.23 in A1). No clear allocator threshold separates fast vs slow regimes.

deterministic_batch_content_shape_effect.rationale: Full-run A1/A2 latency ranks are highly reproducible, but D1-B replay of the same identities collapses historical fast/slow gaps (1↔14 ratio ≈ 0.96; 17↔13 ratio ≈ 1.01). Simple shape correlations in A1 are moderate-to-weak (max seq ≈ 0.46; aggregate tokens ≈ 0.30; padded workload ≈ 0.36; padding fraction ≈ 0).

gpu_device_execution.rationale: A1/A2 wall↔CUDA-device Pearson ≈ 1.0; wall−device residuals are hundreds of ms while slow batches last tens of seconds. The latency explosion is represented in device elapsed time, not host-only wait.

host_scheduling_synchronization.rationale: Near-identity of wall and device times implies host/WSL scheduling outside CUDA work cannot account for the tens-of-seconds stall regime.

power_clock_thermal_state.rationale: SM-clock correlation with latency is weak (~0.27 A1); power draw is approximately uncorrelated; software power-cap is Active on both fast and slow batches; no thermal-throttle Active observations in A1/A2. Temperature associations exist but are confounded with run progression.

state_history_dependent_gpu_model_execut.rationale: Same batch identities are slow in fresh full-index traversals yet ~5 s in controlled one-model targeted replay. Combined with device-time co-location of stalls, this favors a process/run-history dependent GPU/model execution phenomenon over immutable content cost.

unresolved_mixture.rationale: D1 does not isolate a single ultimate GPU root cause; residual mixture among runtime/history effects remains possible.

interpretation_limits: No causal claim solely from correlation.
D1-A/B wall times are attribution-only; not §9.4 10/12-minute gates.
D1 does not promote or modify production policy.
Temperature/run-order confounding prevents thermal causal claims.

d2_eligibility_conditions: Treatments must use controlled repeated-run design.
Process/run history must be controlled; do not interpret a single lucky run.
Lane remains BF16 / CUDA / batch-32 / SDPA unless a later AUTH changes it.
D1 wall times remain attribution-only and are not §9.4 confirmation runs.
scientific_conclusion.summary: D1 execution is valid. Deterministic full-run latency structure is confirmed. Intrinsic batch-content/shape explanation is materially disfavored. Host-only delay is materially disfavored. Simple allocator/clock/thermal explanations are not established. State/history-dependent GPU/model execution remains the leading unresolved class.
